lines.text: Clara tries to count the keys. Somewhere after forty she loses track, starts again, and loses track again.
But don’t bother counting. Look at the black keys instead: twos and threes, all the way along. That’s how pianists find their way.
A true story from music history.
Mozart’s piano had only about five octaves. The full eighty-eight keys came almost a hundred years later.
But the black keys already sat in their twos and threes. The pattern is older than the piano you see today.
Twos and threes. Find the group, and you have found the key.
